minutes.headline: Committee approved the architect RFP with a roll call vote and let the chair make minor legal edits with the procurement officer.
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee finished reviewing the architect and engineering RFP: minimum qualifications, historic preservation experience, scoring rubric, project lead commitment, interviews, selection process and schedule. It voted by roll call to approve the RFP, allowing non-substantive changes required by law. Members also discussed re-engaging the Select Board, Finance Committee, and others before spring Town Meeting funding requests, possibly combined with Turkey Hill.

budget_items.what_was_said: Scoring uses a greater-than threshold for prior project size and count of similar and public projects.

budget_items.what_was_said: The funding request may be combined with School Committee improvements at Turkey Hill as one ask to borrow.

decisions.decision: Minimum requirement added that firms show familiarity and experience with historic architectural preservation; the professional license requirement was kept as required.
Scoring changed to 'greater than' language for project size and count of prior similar and public projects.
Evaluation to require the project lead be part of the interview, with attendance at meetings differentiating the ratings.
Lookback for similar projects extended from five to seven years.
Interview criteria: project lead must be present; all staff in critical roles for the top rating.
Chair will have the procurement officer review the selection/price language to confirm statutory wording, and send the draft to members that night.
RFP must go to the Central Register by Thursday; interviews targeted for Nov 4, first vendor meeting Nov 18.
Committee will spend the next month re-engaging the Select Board (October agenda), Finance Committee, and the APDC before spring Town Meeting.
Next meeting targeted for Monday October 7 at 5:30 p.m., with Brian's minutes added to the agenda.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee approved the architect and engineering RFP by roll call, with the chair allowed to make non-substantive changes required by law.
The RFP now requires firms to show historic preservation experience, and the lookback for similar projects was extended from five to seven years.
Interviews must include the project lead, and the top rating requires all staff in critical roles to attend.
The RFP must reach the Central Register by Thursday, with interviews targeted for Nov 4 and a first vendor meeting Nov 18.
Members plan to spend the next month re-engaging the Select Board, Finance Committee and APDC before a spring Town Meeting funding request, possibly combined with Turkey Hill.

why_it_matters: Hiring the architect starts the design spending that a larger funding request at spring Town Meeting is expected to follow, and a combined borrowing with Turkey Hill would put school and municipal building costs in one vote.
The committee noted that unspent design funds return to the Select Board for reappropriation, so the timing of the hire affects whether the money stays available.
watch_next: Next committee meeting targeted for Monday October 7 at 5:30 p.m.
RFP due at the Central Register by Thursday, with the draft price and selection language to be confirmed by the procurement officer.
